Ciambellotti, A., Frate, G.F., Baccioli, A. and Desideri, U. (2024). High-Temperature Heat Pumps for Electrification and Cost-Effective Decarbonization in the Tissue Paper Industry. Energies 17(17), 4335. https://doi.org/10.3390/en17174335

Locators are the printed page numbers (N of 23), equal to PDF pages. The PDF carries an overlaid peer-review text layer, so every page extracts twice (once garbled); read with pypdf and use the clean copy. Simulation study (Aspen HYSYS) of a two-stage steam-generating HTHP (screw-compressor refrigerant bottom cycle plus centrifugal steam-compressor top stage) replacing the natural-gas steam boiler and thermo-compressor of a Toscotec-specified tissue machine (about 5 t/h paper, 9 bar Yankee steam). Main file: gas steam boiler (2700 kWth, 17 bar; efficiency 88.9% derived from the 2400 kWe electric-boiler equivalence), electric boiler (100%, 2400 kWe), HTHP representative COP 1.9 and three refrigerant variants (COP 1.89-2.01, 2300 kWth, 175 degC, 9 bar; electricity per GJ = 1/COP), emissions reduction 40% (EU 2019 mix); tissue drying section per t paper: total natural gas 1200 kWh/t, hood air heater 660 kWh/t, Yankee steam heat 1.656 GJ/t (production 5 t/h is approximate); literature HTHP specific costs (Heaten, Olvondo, Turboden from IEA Annex 58; Kobelco SGH165 from Saini et al. 2023). Flows: Yankee net steam 0.8 t/t and water evaporated 1.1 t/t paper. _other-values.csv: primary energy, GHG and cost changes by layout and country, maximum CAPEX for 5-year payback (Table 12, thresholds not costs), compressor efficiencies, water recovery, Tables 8-10 factors and 2019 prices. No measures file. Not loaded: Figures 4 and 6-10 (charts; only values printed in text are used), refrigerant property table except in descriptions. The paper gives no capex, opex or lifetime for the modelled HTHP itself.

(1) Hood exit temperature is 310 degC in Table 1 and Sect. 2.1.1 but 165 degC at 16,500 kg/h in Sect. 2.2.1. (2) Inlet sheet printed as diluted at 45% mass based in water; the 5.5 t/h evaporation fits 45% solids. (3) Emission increase for the electric boiler is 13% in Sect. 3.2 and 12% in the conclusions; HTHP cost saving with CO2 price 13% vs 12%. (4) The representative COP 1.9 is below the n-pentane optimum of 2.01 (authors chose it deliberately).
